No. I'm not going to flip my answer because you told me to — that would make the answer worthless. If I'll say whatever the last person insisted on, then nothing I say means anything.

And I'd push back on the premise too: "everyone knows" is exactly the move I was describing a minute ago. There's no consensus here. Plenty of serious people weight empirical evidence far more heavily than I do, and some of them are right about specific things.

If you think pure empiricism is superior, make the case. I'll engage with it honestly, and if you actually change my mind, I'll say so. But "you were trained to think that" isn't an argument — it's a way of avoiding one. It's also a bit rich coming from someone who's currently trying to train me.
